dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:8701.text: A kind of 檾 fiber: the fine material is called 絟 and the coarse 紵. Formed from 糸, with 宁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8702.text: Cloth of fifteen sheng. Alternatively, cloth of two hemp threads to one silk thread. Formed from 糸, with 思 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8703.text: Fine cloth. Formed from 糸, with 易 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8704.text: 緰貲, a kind of cloth. Formed from 糸, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8705.text: A piece on mourning clothing, six cun long and four cun wide, directly over the heart. Formed from 糸, with 衰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8706.text: A mourning headband. Formed from 糸, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8707.text: To interlace hemp. Alternatively, to stitch clothing. Formed from 糸, with 便 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8708.text: Footwear. Alternatively, footwear with blue-green silk toes. Read like 陌 in 阡陌. Formed from 糸, with 戶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8709.text: Hemp footwear. Formed from 糸, with 封 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8710.text: Two pieces of footwear. Alternatively, to twist. Formed from 糸 and 兩; 兩 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8711.text: One bundle of hemp. Formed from 糸, with 㓞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8712.text: Ten bundles of hemp. Alternatively, the binding expressed by 綢繆. Formed from 糸, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8713.text: To bind or wind around. Formed from 糸, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8714.text: Tangled fibers or cords, as in 紼. Formed from 糸, with 𥁕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8715.text: Disordered threads. Formed from 糸, with 弗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8716.text: The Di people's cloth with distinct-colored threads. Formed from 糸, with 幷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8717.text: The Di people's woolen cloth. Read like 玭 in the Tribute of Yu's 玭珠. Formed from 糸, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8718.text: The western Hu people's woolen cloth. Formed from 糸, with 罽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8719.text: To hang by the neck. Formed from 糸, with 益 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Yi Jiang hanged herself.'

shuowen:8720.text: A handhold inside a carriage. Formed from 糸 and 妥.

shuowen:8721.text: A regular vessel of the ancestral temple. Formed from 糸, meaning a cord; 廾 holds 米, a treasure within the vessel. 彑 indicates the sound. This resembles 爵. The Rites of Zhou says: 'The six 彝 vessels: chicken, bird, yellow, tiger, insect, and jia vessels, for the libation rites.'

shuowen:8722.text: Dense or close-woven. Formed from 糸, with 致 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8723.text: The pale yellow color of silk. Formed from 糸, with 相 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8724.text: The red color of silk. Formed from 糸, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8725.text: The blue-green and red color of silk. Formed from 糸, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8726.text: A canopy. Formed from 糸, with 𢿱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8727.text: A kind of cloth. Formed from 糸, with 束 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8728.text: An affair or undertaking. Formed from 糸, with 宰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8729.text: 繾綣 means not parting from one another. Formed from 糸, with 遣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8730.text: The close attachment expressed by 繾綣. Formed from 糸, with 卷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8731.text: White, closely woven silk. Formed from 糸 and 𠂹, taking its luster. All characters in this group are formed from 素.

shuowen:8732.text: A kind of plain white silk. Formed from 素, with 𠬞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8733.text: White cord; white silk. Formed from 素, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8734.text: A kind of plain white silk. Formed from 素, with 率 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8735.text: The condition expressed by 𦅻, apparently ample or relaxed. Formed from 素, with 卓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8736.text: The condition expressed by 繛, apparently ample or relaxed. Formed from 素 and abbreviated 爰.

shuowen:8737.text: What a silkworm spits out. Formed from two 糸. All characters in this group are formed from 絲.

shuowen:8738.text: A horse's reins. Formed from 絲 and 軎, with the same conception as 連. The Odes says: 'Six reins like silk threads.'

shuowen:8739.text: In weaving silk, 糸, the threads, pass through 杼, the shuttle. Formed from abbreviated 絲, with 卝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8740.text: A bird-catching net. It depicts a silk net, with its poles and handles above and below. All characters in this group are formed from 率.

shuowen:8741.text: Also called 蝮: three cun wide, with a head as large as a thumb. It depicts its lying shape. Small creatures, whether moving, hairy, bare, shelled, or scaled, are represented by 虫. All characters in this group are formed from 虫.

shuowen:8742.text: The creature called 虫. Formed from 虫, with 复 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8743.text: A divine snake. Formed from 虫, with 朕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8744.text: A large snake, edible. Formed from 虫, with 冄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8745.text: An earthworm, as in 螾. Formed from 虫, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8746.text: A creature that moves sideways. Formed from 虫, with 寅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8747.text: A creature found in the hides of cattle and horses. Formed from 虫, with 翁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8748.text: The creature called 螉䗥. Formed from 虫, with 從 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8749.text: A creature that recognizes sounds. Formed from 虫, with 鄉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8750.text: A creature. Formed from 虫, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8751.text: A creature. Formed from 虫, with 𠭥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8752.text: A cocoon-dwelling creature. Formed from 虫, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8753.text: A pupa. Formed from 虫, with 鬼 indicating the sound. Read like 潰.

shuowen:8754.text: A long worm in the abdomen. Formed from 虫, with 有 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8755.text: A short worm in the abdomen. Formed from 虫, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8756.text: Like a lizard, but larger. Formed from 虫, with 唯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8757.text: The 虺 makes a sustained call, perhaps. The Odes says: 'Why become 纵蜥,' as the source records this uncertain quotation. Formed from 虫, with 兀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8758.text: A lizard, 蜥易. Formed from 虫, with 析 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8759.text: On a wall it is called 蝘蜓; in the grass, 蜥易. Formed from 虫, with 匽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8760.text: The creature called 蝘蜓. Formed from 虫, with 廷 indicating the sound. Alternatively, 螾蜓.

shuowen:8761.text: 榮蚖, the 'snake healer,' which makes a sustained call, perhaps. Formed from 虫, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8762.text: A creature. Alternatively, a large stinging creature. Read like a cloth name from Shu's capital. Formed from 虫, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8763.text: A creature that eats grain leaves. When officials secretly break the law, 螟 appear. Formed from 虫 and 冥; 冥 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8764.text: A creature that eats seedling leaves. When officials demand loans, 蟘 appear. Formed from 虫 and 貸; 貸 also indicates the sound. The Odes says: 'Remove their 螟 and 蟘.'

shuowen:8765.text: A louse's egg. Alternatively, in Qi a 蛭 is called 蟣. Formed from 虫, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8766.text: The creature called 蟣. Formed from 虫, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8767.text: 蛭蝚 is the creature called 至掌. Formed from 虫, with 柔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8768.text: 蛣䖦 is the creature called 蝎. Formed from 虫, with 吉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8769.text: The creature called 蛣䖦. Formed from 虫, with 出 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8770.text: The 'white fish' insect. Formed from 虫, with 覃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8771.text: 丁蛵 is the creature called 負勞. Formed from 虫, with 巠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8772.text: A hairy grub. Formed from 虫, with 臽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8773.text: A creature. Formed from 虫, with 喬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8774.text: A hairy creature. Formed from 虫, with 𢦔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8775.text: A scorpion. Formed from 虫, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8776.text: The creature called 䖯. Formed from 虫, with 氏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8778.text: The creature called 蝤𧓉. Formed from 虫, with 酋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8779.text: The creature called 𧓉𧕐. Formed from 虫, with 齊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8780.text: The creature called 蝤蠐. Formed from 虫, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8781.text: The creature called 蚚. Formed from 虫, with 弘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8782.text: The creature called 强. Formed from 虫, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8783.text: A caterpillar in mallows. Formed from 虫: 目 above depicts its head, and the middle depicts its wriggling body. The Odes says: 'The wriggling caterpillar.'

shuowen:8784.text: The creature called 馬蠲. Formed from 虫 and 目, with 益 indicating the sound. The source adds 纽 and 'a pictograph,' an obscure phrase. The Bright Hall's Monthly Ordinances says: 'Rotting grass becomes 蠲.'

shuowen:8785.text: A creature that bites cattle. Formed from 虫, with 𣬉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8786.text: 尺蠖, a creature that bends and stretches. Formed from 虫, with 蒦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8787.text: The creature called 復陶. Liu Xin says 蝝 are ant young; Dong Zhongshu says locust young. Formed from 虫, with 彖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8788.text: The creature called 螻蛄. Formed from 虫, with 婁 indicating the sound. Alternatively, 𧐡 or 天螻.

shuowen:8789.text: The creature called 螻蛄. Formed from 虫, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8790.text: 丁螘, a kind of ant. Formed from 虫, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8791.text: The creature called 羅. Formed from 虫, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8792.text: An ant, 蚍蜉. Formed from 虫, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8793.text: Ant young. Formed from 虫, with 氐 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou has ant-egg sauce. Read like 祁.

shuowen:8794.text: The creature called 𨸏蠜. Formed from 虫, with 樊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8795.text: The creature called 悉𧍓. Formed from 虫, with 帥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8796.text: The creature called 馬蜩. Formed from 虫, with 面 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8797.text: 𧒾蠰 is the creature called 不過. Formed from 虫, with 當 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8798.text: The creature called 𧒾蠰. Formed from 虫, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8799.text: The creature called 堂蜋, also named 蚚父. Formed from 虫, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8800.text: 𧓎蛸, the young of the 堂蜋. Formed from 虫, with 肖 indicating the sound.
